content.title: About
content.content: Seven and Seven is a non‑alcoholic mix of tonic water and lemon‑lime soda, popular in the United States as a refreshing beverage. It combines the mild bitterness of tonic with a bright citrus note, making it ideal for summer gatherings and mocktails.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first Seven and Seven recipe appeared in the 1970s in California bars.
The name comes from the combination of the 7UP and Seagram’s Seven brands, although the original mix is often made with other tonics.
The drink is commonly served over ice with a lime wedge to enhance flavor.
In the 1990s, Seven and Seven became a popular non‑alcoholic cocktail option in school cafeterias.

items.title: Alcohol‑free
items.content: Because the drink contains no alcohol, it is suitable for children and individuals who avoid alcohol.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: The lemon juice provides a modest amount of vitamin C, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Water and tonic help maintain fluid balance, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Traditional recipes use sugary syrup, which can be problematic for people with diabetes or those watching calorie intake.

items.title: Caffeine in tonic
items.content: Some tonic waters contain measurable caffeine, which may affect sleep.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Lemon juice raises the drink’s acidity, potentially irritating sensitive teeth or stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Combine 1 part 7UP (or a similar lemon‑lime soda) with 1 part tonic water, add ice and a lime wedge. Feel free to adjust proportions or substitute tonic with sparkling water flavored with lemon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared mix in a sealed bottle in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours to retain freshness and aroma. Do not leave opened tonic at room temperature for more than 2 days.
